channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Dark Matter acquires House Numbers' mortgage AI agents and names its founder chief AI officer
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Dark Matter Technologies said on October 30 it has acquired the AI agent platform of House Numbers, in production for two years across more than 100 lenders, and brought on co-founder Jeff Levinsohn as chief AI officer. Terms were not disclosed.

item.title: Cohere says its Canada bet now totals C$4 billion and 1,500 jobs by 2031
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cohere said on October 30 its multi-year Canadian investment effort, underway since 2024, is now expected to top C$4 billion and add more than 1,500 jobs by 2031 — a progress update that landed a day after Ottawa pledged up to C$1.6 billion for a stake in the company.

item.title: Blackstone warns Anthropic may land a junk credit rating after its IPO, reversing its investment-grade call
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Blackstone has told investors Anthropic is likely to receive a double-B credit rating after its IPO, the Financial Times reported on October 30 — a reversal that could raise the cost of funding Anthropic’s planned $800 billion-plus infrastructure buildout.

item.title: Soup hands-on: fine-tune an LLM from a single YAML file, from first config to a working adapter
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Soup is a command-line tool that collapses LLM fine-tuning into one YAML file and one command — and its layer streaming trains an 8B model on a 4 GB laptop GPU. This guide installs Soup, writes a real training config, trains a LoRA adapter on CPU, and proves the adapter changed the model's answers.

item.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Bing back a single robots.txt signal for AI training preferences
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: For years, telling AI companies not to train on your site meant maintaining a separate rule for every crawler. On October 30, the biggest AI providers agreed to honor one shared signal instead — a small file change with large consequences for publishers.

item.title: Google's Suncatcher satellite answers its first prompt from orbit — with a haiku from a TPU in space
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google said on October 30 that its Project Suncatcher prototype returned the first AI response from a data-center-class TPU in orbit: a Gemma 4 haiku, downlinked as the satellite passed Svalbard. The test shows the chip can run in space; whether orbital data centers make economic sense is still unproven.

item.title: Your agent should brief you first: run OpenDuet, the self-hosted proactive agent
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenDuet is CopilotKit's open-source template for a proactive agent: it triages Gmail and calendar, delivers a morning brief, and keeps working on a computer of its own, asking before it sends, pays, signs, or deletes. This guide runs it locally with Docker and Bun, tries it safely with the built-in fake Google account, and shows how to make it your own — 1,633 stars in its first nine days, MIT-licensed, and still early development.

item.title: Sam Altman calls local AI inference a 'terrible' use of scarce DRAM — and the local-model community pushed back
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI's chief executive argued on a podcast that running AI on personal computers wastes the world's scarce memory. The local-model community heard something else: an argument about who gets to own the machines intelligence runs on.

item.title: Your fine-tune is only as good as its data: build a clean SFT dataset from your own documents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Most fine-tuning failures are data failures, not model failures: this guide turns a folder of draft examples into a validated, deduplicated, leakage-checked SFT dataset — train/validation split included — with Python's standard library alone, every check run and every number real.

item.title: OpenAI to publish a Community Safety Report and restrict weapons information for teens
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI said on October 30 it will publish a Community Safety Report on violence prevention, with the first edition in early 2027 covering the second half of 2026. It also tightened how ChatGPT answers questions about past mass attacks and restricted weapons-related information for under-18s, after making more than 200 law-enforcement referrals in the third quarter of 2026.

item.title: Musk and Zuckerberg swap 'AI' for 'super intelligence' on earnings calls — while Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet stick with AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: On their third-quarter earnings calls, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg adopted President Trump’s preferred term ‘super intelligence’ — but their peers at Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet did not. The split says less about vocabulary than about who wants to be heard agreeing with the White House, and who is careful not to be.

item.title: One operator, 200 targets: CrowdStrike says AI agents ran a global espionage campaign
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: CrowdStrike says a China-linked group used the ARTEX agent framework to run intrusions against more than 200 organizations in 11 days, with a single human operator steering the agents at decision points. Nine organizations were confirmed breached.

item.title: Ares Intelligence raises €2.9 million to ask every employee where AI fits — starting with the front line, not the C-suite
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: London startup Ares Intelligence has raised €2.9 million from Creandum and Lakestar for an AI interviewer that holds confidential voice conversations with every employee — in more than 70 languages — and turns what they say into a prioritised AI adoption roadmap within weeks.

item.title: Nanobot hands-on: run a 4,000-line personal agent on your own machine
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Nanobot is a self-hosted personal AI agent with a roughly 4,000-line Python core: this guide installs 0.4.0, points it at a local Ollama model, proves the file read/write loop, and documents honestly where a 0.6B model fails and where this sandbox blocked the WebUI.

item.title: INSEAD launches Thrive Lab with $3 million from Google.org and DeepMind — to study how people flourish alongside AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: INSEAD announced on October 30, 2026 that Google.org and Google DeepMind will fund its new Thrive Lab with US$3 million, to research how people and organisations can flourish — in learning, work, and relationships — as AI reshapes daily life.

item.title: Envision’s Tianji tops ECMWF’s AI Weather Quest: a physics-AI model aimed at the 19–25 day window
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Envision announced on October 30, 2026 that its Tianji weather foundation model ranked first overall in ECMWF’s AI Weather Quest, beating nearly 20 teams across every assessed metric for days 19–25 — the subseasonal window where forecasts get hardest, and where wind and solar planning lives.

item.title: Reddit says Google's AI Mode sends it no traffic — and will test locking casual browsing behind a login
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Reddit's search referrals fell by more than a million a week in October, its US audience shrank for the first time since its IPO, and its answer is to test a mostly logged-in site — trading reach for control over the community archive that AI companies want to scrape.

item.title: Lightpanda hands-on: the headless browser built for AI agents, from first fetch to a replayable scrape
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Lightpanda is a headless browser written from scratch in Zig for agents and automation — no Chromium, a fraction of the memory. This guide installs the nightly binary, fetches JavaScript-rendered pages to Markdown, extracts structured data, and turns a REPL session into a replayable script you can run without any model at all.

item.title: Point your coding agent at your repo and get a threat model you can actually check: hands-on with Grim Prompter
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Grim Prompter (jmanico/grim-prompter, MIT, 212 GitHub stars) turns Claude Code, Codex or any coding agent into a threat-model reviewer: 36 architecture workflows and 29 method prompts, installed by linking one skill, run with a single slash command, and checked against your code with file-and-line citations. This guide installs it, runs a quick API model, challenges the findings, and keeps the model current as the code changes.

item.title: Cognizant commits more than 25,000 professionals to OpenAI delivery with a new Frontier Capability Group
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cognizant announced on October 30, 2026 that it has formed an OpenAI Frontier Capability Group of more than 25,000 professionals to deliver Codex and ChatGPT into enterprise software, modernization, and customer operations — starting with methods it tested inside its own sales teams.

item.title: A six-year-old designed a unicorn game and Claude Sonnet built it in under a month — Reddit's verdict on the father-daughter build
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A father and his six-year-old daughter designed a pixel-art unicorn sandbox together, with Claude Sonnet 5.5 writing the code — and a 2:33 gameplay clip has r/ClaudeAI debating what, exactly, deserves the amazement.

item.title: Your laptop is the API: run a local LLM server with llama-cpp-python and a 398 MB GGUF model
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: llama-cpp-python turns a 398 MB GGUF model into a local OpenAI-compatible API: this guide loads Qwen2.5-0.5B on CPU, streams tokens, forces JSON-schema output, and serves it on localhost — with every command verified and one honest model failure included.

item.title: Waymo’s next robotaxi is a Toyota: factory-built bZ4X fleet to test in Japan in 2027, UK to follow
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Toyota and Waymo will begin testing a fleet of autonomous Toyota bZ4X SUVs in Japan in 2027, built and fitted with Waymo’s driving hardware at Toyota’s Takaoka plant, with deployment in the UK and other Waymo markets planned for later years.

item.title: OpenAI rewrites its Model Spec around five values — and admits its models do not follow it yet
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI has rewritten the public rulebook for how its models should behave, organizing it around five values headed by faithfulness to human intent. The document now also spells out hard limits on autonomous agents — and, in the same breath, concedes that today’s models do not live up to it yet.

item.title: Blind the agent reading your code: hands-on with BLA, the open-source shield against AI reverse-engineering
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: BLA, a five-day-old MIT-licensed shield created on October 25, 2026, hardens your shipped JavaScript against AI reverse-engineering agents: one audit, one protect command, and the demo file's exposure score fell from 81 to 2 while its output stayed identical. This guide runs every command and shows the real numbers, including the caveats.
